title: What is the KPMG consulting interview process, and how should you prepare?
description: How KPMG consulting tends to hire: online assessments, competency interviews, case studies and group simulations, and how to prepare.
hook: KPMG's consulting process usually runs from an online application to online tests, a recorded or live interview, and a final assessment that mixes an interview with group or written work. Behavioural questions carry more weight than at MBB, and cases tend to be shorter and more practical. The exact stages depend on the country, the service line and your level, so read your invitation closely.
body:
How the process usually runs

KPMG is a network of member firms, and each one runs its own recruiting. The UK graduate route is the clearest published example. As of the 2026 to 2027 intake, KPMG UK's own careers site lists four stages:

StageWhat happensWhat it tests
Explore and applyAn unassessed job preview quiz, then an application formEligibility and fit with the programme
Online assessmentsAn untimed skills assessment (allow about 20 minutes) and a 36-minute cognitive test of numerical and logical reasoningJudgement at work, speed and accuracy with numbers
Video interviewSix pre-recorded questions, answered on camera, with set preparation timeMotivation, strengths and how clearly you speak
Launch PadA half-day, in-person event of assessed and non-assessed activities; offers follow within two working days if you succeedTeamwork, analysis and a final judgement on fit

KPMG UK asks you to complete the assessments without help from other people or AI tools, and may re-test parts of them later. Our guide to online tests covers how to build speed on numerical reasoning.

Elsewhere the shape changes: experienced hires usually start with a recruiter call, then meet managers and directors. Your invitation is the only reliable guide to your own process.

Behavioural questions built on KPMG's values

KPMG's published values are Integrity, Excellence, Courage, Together and For Better. Interviewers do not expect you to recite them, but your stories should show them. Prepare six to eight stories: teamwork, a hard decision, learning fast, a mistake, influencing someone and a result you are proud of. Use a simple situation, task, action, result shape and spend most of the time on what you did.

Here is the difference on a common question, "Tell me about a time you worked as part of a team."

Weak: "We had a group project and everyone worked really well together. We communicated a lot and got a good mark."
Strong: "Our four-person dissertation group was two weeks behind because two of us were redoing the same analysis. I suggested we split the work by chapter and hold a ten-minute check-in each morning. We caught up in eight days and submitted on time. I learned to agree who owns what before anyone starts."

The strong answer shows Together and Excellence without naming them. Our list of common fit questions covers the rest of the set.

Every round also includes some version of "Why KPMG?" Name the service line, say what you learned from someone in the firm or its published work, and link it to something you have done. "It is a big brand" is not an answer.

Cases at KPMG: shorter and more practical

Where KPMG uses cases, they tend to be shorter and more operational than a classic MBB case. You are more likely to be asked why a process got slower than whether to enter China. Here is the kind of reasoning that does well.

Prompt: a bank's call centre handles 80,000 calls a month. Average handling time has risen from five to six minutes. What does that cost, and what would you look at?

  1. Size the change. Workload has gone from 80,000 × 5 = 400,000 minutes to 80,000 × 6 = 480,000 minutes a month. That is 80,000 extra minutes, or about 1,333 hours, a 20% increase with no extra calls.
  2. Turn it into people. At 120 productive hours per agent per month, 1,333 ÷ 120 ≈ 11 extra full-time agents, before allowing for absence or peaks.
  3. Turn it into money. At an illustrative $4,000 a month per agent, fully loaded, that is about $44k a month, or roughly $530k a year.
  4. Find the cause. A new call mix, an extra verification step, a slower system or less training for new joiners? Ask for handling time by call type and agent tenure.
  5. Recommend a test. Pilot the fix with one team and track handling time and repeat calls. A shorter call that makes the customer ring back has not saved anything.

That last point is what interviewers listen for: you have tied the number to an operational decision. For more of this style, see the complete guide to operations cases.

How to stand out in a group exercise

Assessors watch how you work with others as much as your ideas. Build on other people's points, keep time, bring the discussion back to the question and bring quieter people in. Talking over people, or going silent, gets you marked down. Our guide to group and written cases has a full time plan.

Common mistakes

  • Preparing only cases. At KPMG the behavioural and video stages screen out more people than candidates expect. Rehearse your stories out loud, on camera, to time.
  • Stopping at the number. In operational cases, always say what the number means for the client and what you would test next.

Practise now

1. An invoice team processes 30,000 invoices a month at 12 minutes each. Automation can handle 40% of them at 2 minutes each. How many hours a month are saved, and roughly how many people is that at 140 productive hours each?

Show the answer

40% of 30,000 is 12,000 invoices. Each saves 12 − 2 = 10 minutes, so 120,000 minutes, or 2,000 hours a month. 2,000 ÷ 140 ≈ 14 people. At an illustrative $3,500 a month each, that is about $50k a month, or $600k a year, before the cost of the software and the risk of errors on the automated invoices.

2. In a group exercise, two candidates spend ten minutes arguing about one data point. What do you say?

Show the answer

Something like: "Both views are useful. Can we note that as a risk, agree it does not change the recommendation either way, and move to the costs so we leave ten minutes to prepare?" You have respected both people, kept time and steered back to the decision.

Where to practise next

Compare KPMG with its peers in our guide to the Big Four, then build case speed with the maths drills. Details here were checked in November 2026; processes change by office and year, so always confirm with your recruiter.
